description: Join us! Seeking coders, 3D artists, data analysts, UI/UX designers, and space research enthusiasts.
summary:
Problem Statement
Important scientific and engineering contributions of abandoned space equipment are often overlooked. School-age learners may know about famous NASA missions without understanding the hardware that made those missions possible or the scientific knowledge they generated.

Proposed Solution
An interactive digital museum documenting NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

Key Features
- Destination-based exploration: Moon and Mars.
- Equipment profiles describing purpose, mission history and current status.
- Historical mission timelines.
- Scientific discoveries associated with each piece of equipment.
- NASA imagery and references supporting the stories.
- Educational storytelling designed for younger audiences.

Target Audience
School-age students, educators, space enthusiasts and people interested in planetary science.

Expected Impact
- Improve accessibility of space science education.
- Encourage curiosity about planetary exploration.
- Communicate the engineering behind historic missions.
- Preserve the scientific legacy of equipment left beyond Earth.

Team
- Anubhuti Goswami – B.Tech Biotechnology
- Likitha – B.Tech CSE (AI/ML)
- Tamanya – MCA Core
details: The project is an educational, interactive web platform focused on space science, astronomy, and science communication. Developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with JSON as its data format, the platform operates as a static website without a backend and is hosted on GitHub Pages. It features three main learning chapters: Moon, Mars, and Deep Space, supported by an almanac and linked factual records to provide reliable scientific information. Interactive learning tools include quizzes, mission-matching activities, and arcade-style games, while engagement features such as planet collection and certificate generation encourage exploration and learning.
